THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.
Both the insurer as well as the claimants are in appeal.

2. The Tribunal has recorded a finding that both the rider of the motor cycle and the driver of the lorry were equally responsible for the accident and has attributed negligence in the ratio of 50:50.
The Tribunal in order to come to this conclusion has relied upon the fact that the chargesheet had been laid against both the rider of the two wheeler and the driver of the lorry.

3. Learned counsel for the insurer contends that since the rider of the motor cycle was also chargesheeted, it would be appropriate to attribute negligence entirely on the rider of the motor cycle, whereas the counsel for the claimant contends that since the Tribunal has recorded a clear finding that there was negligence on the part of the lorry driver in stopping the lorry suddenly in the middle of the road.
The Tribunal ought to have held that the driver of the lorry alone was responsible for the accident.
It is no doubt true that a chargesheet was laid against both the rider of the two wheeler as well as the driver of the lorry.
4. The Tribunal taking into consideration these facts and also the oral evidence adduced has recorded the following finding :

"The contents of charge-sheet also discloses that, on the alleged date of accident, the claimant being the rider of his Activa Honda bearing No.KA-06-EG-5165 has driven the same in rash and negligence manner on the said road even though there was sufficient space for passing his vehicle on the said road and dashed to the lorry from its behind.

So it appears that, the Lorry driver has negligently stopped his vehicle on the middle of the road without giving any signals to the other vehicles and at the same time, it is the duty of the claimant to see the vehicles in front of him and drove his vehicle cautiously.
However, the claimant has drove his vehicle in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the said lorry from its behind and caused accident.

Therefore, I am come to the conclusion that, the alleged accident occurred not only due to the rash and negligent act of the lorry driver but due to the contributory negligence on the part of the claimant also and both the drivers of vehicles involved in the accident have contributed the same degree of negligence in the alleged accident."

3 5.

The fact that the Tribunal has recorded a clear finding that a lorry driver has negligently stopped the vehicle in the middle of the road without giving any signal to other vehicles itself is sufficient to come to the conclusion that the negligence was entirely on the part of the lorry driver.

If the lorry driver was suddenly to stop in the middle of the road, the possibility of an accident occurring would be very high since the vehicle coming behind would not be able to anticipate that, the lorry would suddenly stop on a highway.
6. It may also be pertinent to state that the driver of the lorry was not examined to establish that the lorry had been safely parked and the parked lorry was feasible to vehicles coming from behind.

7. In the light of the finding recorded by the Tribunal that the lorry driver had negligently stopped in the middle of the road, the apportionment of 50% negligence on the rider of the two-wheeler cannot be sustained and same is accordingly set aside.
8. It has to be held that the driver of the lorry was alone responsible for the accident and as a consequence the insurer of the lorry would be liable to satisfy the compensation.

9. As far as compensation is concerned, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- towards 'pain and sufferings', Rs.20,000/- towards 'conveyance and attendant charges', Rs.20,000/-
towards 'loss of comforts and amenities', apart from the medical expenses of Rs.7,30,000/-.
10. In my view, the sums awarded under all the heads are just and proper and do not call for any enhancement.
11. The appeal filed by claimant, insofar as enhancement of compensation is concerned, is dismissed.
12. The appeal filed by insurer is accordingly disposed of.
13. It is also made clear that the insurer would be liable to pay the compensation awarded by the Tribunal in its entirety to the claimant.
14. The disbursement of the amount shall be in terms of the Award of the Tribunal.
